title: Simultaneous local and global bounds for confluently persistent tries
formal: Can the functional trie representations of Demaine, Langerman and Price be combined so that modifying a node at depth \(d\) costs \(O(1+\min\{d\log(2+\Delta),\log(2+n)\})\) time and permanent space, while preserving their navigation and subtree-copy interface? Here \(n\) is the number of logical nodes of the modified version and \(\Delta\) bounds the relevant trie degrees.
definitions: A trie is a rooted tree with distinct ordered labels on the outgoing edges of each node and constant-size data at each node. Versions remain available, including both sources of a subtree copy. There are a fixed constant number of fingers per version. Navigation places a finger at the root, moves to its parent or follows a child edge of a supplied label. Updates change node data, insert or delete a leaf, copy a subtree from one version into another, or remove a subtree. A functional pointer representation may allocate initialized records but cannot overwrite old records. Logical nodes can share physical representation, so logical version size differs from total allocated space. The source distinguishes temporary records allocated during navigation from those retained by a subsequent modification; that distinction affects the proposed minimum bound.
why: The question concerns whether persistent hierarchical data can exploit shallow or local changes while also protecting users against arbitrarily deep versions.

context_blocks.text: The locality-sensitive representation allocates records during navigation; those records can become permanent when a modification commits them. The globally balanced representation instead has logarithmic update space with navigation using no permanent space.

Section 6 explicitly asks for the minimum of local-depth and global-size costs. Treating the first representation as already having both guarantees overlooks navigation space retained by later updates.
